bibliography.title: MC-Search: Evaluating and Enhancing Multimodal Agentic Search with Structured Long Reasoning Chains

sections.title: 3 Agentic MM-RAG Pipeline and Process-Level Alignment
Appendix M Theoretical Justification of Topology Designs

abstract_sentences.text: With the increasing demand for step-wise, cross-modal, and knowledge-grounded reasoning, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are evolving beyond the traditional fixed retrieve-then-generate paradigm toward more sophisticated agentic multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (MM-RAG).

evidence.anchor: MLLMs evolve toward agentic multimodal RAG

abstract_sentences.text: Existing benchmarks, however, mainly focus on simplified QA with short retrieval chains, leaving adaptive planning and multimodal reasoning underexplored.

evidence.anchor: existing benchmarks focus on simplified QA and short chains

abstract_sentences.text: We present MC-SEARCH, the first benchmark for agentic MM-RAG with long, step-wise annotated reasoning chains spanning five representative reasoning structures.

evidence.anchor: first benchmark with five representative reasoning structures

abstract_sentences.text: Each example specifies sub-questions, retrieval modalities, supporting facts, and intermediate answers, with fidelity ensured by HAVE (Hop-wise Attribution and Verification of Evidence), resulting in 3,333 high-quality examples averaging 3.7 hops.
Beyond answer accuracy, MC-SEARCH introduces new process-level metrics for reasoning quality, stepwise retrieval and planning accuracy.
By developing a unified agentic MM-RAG pipeline, we benchmark six leading MLLMs and reveal systematic issues such as over- and under-retrieval and modality-misaligned planning.

evidence.anchor: six leading MLLMs and over/under-retrieval issues

abstract_sentences.text: Finally, we introduce SEARCH-ALIGN, a process-supervised fine-tuning framework leveraging verified reasoning chains, showing that our data not only enables faithful evaluation but also improves planning and retrieval fidelity in open-source MLLMs.

evidence.anchor: SEARCH-ALIGN improves planning and retrieval fidelity
MLLMs move from text-only inputs to interleaved cross-modal contexts
complex queries require multi-step cross-modal reasoning
three limitations: fixed pipeline, short hops, missing stepwise topology
MC-SEARCH pairs each question with a golden step-wise trajectory
five structures and HAVE are previewed
process metrics and six-model findings are previewed
SEARCH-ALIGN provides process supervision for open-source models
Benchmark, Metrics, Evaluation, and Method contribution bullets
MM-RAG benchmarks classified by pipeline, caption, hop length, annotation
multimodal benchmark limits are separated into four dimensions
structure-aware work focuses on what to retrieve, while this work supervises chain structure
G(Q,A) contains q_t, m_t, r_t, and a_t
long verified chains address shallow VQA benchmarks
Wikipedia clusters and Gemini-2.5-Flash generate approximately 21k examples
Util(t) is defined by the F1 drop after removing r_t
Nav(t) checks entities in downstream sub-questions
Qwen filtering, Gemini hop shrinkage, and HAVE redundancy check
unused evidence is filtered to enforce a unique reasoning graph
F1, delta F1, Golden F1, and LLJ are introduced
HPS and RD align predicted and golden graphs
three pipeline modules iterate planning, retrieval, and synthesis
SEARCH-ALIGN turns verified chains into conversation-level SFT traces

result_inventory.claim: MC-SEARCH contains a large, topology-balanced multimodal benchmark.
result_inventory.value: 3,333 samples; 3.79 average hops; topology counts 1,306/945/680/233/169.
result_inventory.comparison: Five reasoning graphs; Image-Initiated is largest and Text-Initiated smallest.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Descriptive counts and averages; no interval or hypothesis test.

result_inventory.claim: The filtered chains receive high quality scores.
result_inventory.value: Factual 4.93, necessity 4.70, clarity 4.88, multimodal alignment 4.95, overall 4.87/5.
result_inventory.comparison: Four dimensions scored by Gemini-2.5-Pro.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Mean of integer 1–5 scores; no uncertainty reported.

result_inventory.claim: Gemini-2.5-Pro is a strong backbone on most topologies.
result_inventory.value: Image-Initiated F1 47.61, HPS 25.90, RD 1.05, Golden F1 69.83.
result_inventory.comparison: Backbone rows in Table 3 across five graphs.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Sample-level aggregate F1/HPS/RD/Golden F1 and LLJ; no significance test.

result_inventory.claim: SEARCH-ALIGN improves open-source answer and chain alignment metrics.
result_inventory.value: InternVL approximately +2.8 F1/+12.0 HPS/RD −0.6; Qwen +13.7 F1/+16.0 HPS/RD −3.1.
result_inventory.comparison: Before/after average across topologies.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Differences of aggregate metrics; no seed-level variance or significance test.

result_inventory.claim: Parallel Image-Text Fork is the hardest topology.
result_inventory.value: All backbones reach their lowest F1 and HPS on this topology.
result_inventory.comparison: Compared with Image-Initiated, Text-Initiated, Text-Only and Multi-Images graphs.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Cross-topology descriptive comparison in Table 3.

evidence.anchor: parallel fork has lowest F1 and HPS

result_inventory.claim: Longer chains degrade model performance.
result_inventory.value: F1 drops sharply at 4–5 hops relative to 1–3 hops.
result_inventory.comparison: All six model curves in Figure 3.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Descriptive curve comparison; no fitted model or uncertainty.

evidence.anchor: consistent drop as chain length increases

result_inventory.claim: Moderate over-retrieval can help, while severe under/over-retrieval harms.

result_inventory.comparison: Model curves across ΔStep in Figure 4.

result_inventory.statistical_method: Covered/gold step counts and percentages.

result_inventory.claim: Retrieval and planning failures dominate the eight-way error taxonomy.
result_inventory.value: Retrieval-Failure 84.70%, Hallucinated-Entity/Attribute 75.75%, Step-Omission 74.34%; Evidence-Misinterpretation 8.35%.
result_inventory.comparison: Eight error categories annotated by Gemini-2.5-Pro.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Proportion of samples; no uncertainty or inter-annotator interval.

result_inventory.claim: Single-step retrieval is an information bottleneck for long chains.
result_inventory.value: Image-Initiated Gemini-Pro F1 2.34/LLJ 0.13; Qwen F1 40.31/LLJ 1.62.
result_inventory.comparison: Fixed one-step top-1 RAG across model families.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate F1/LLJ under confidence-based abstention; no interval.

result_inventory.comparison: Single-step Table 5 and agentic Table 3.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Descriptive baseline comparison.

result_inventory.claim: LLJ scores are consistent across model families.

result_inventory.comparison: Qwen before vs after alignment across k.
result_inventory.statistical_method: Aggregate F1, ΔF1, HPS and RD.

claim_closure.claim: MC-SEARCH supplies long, step-wise, cross-modal benchmark chains.
claim_closure.method_response: Five graph topologies and golden (q,m,r,a) chains are defined.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2/Table 7 and Appendix C give counts, statistics and examples.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates structured step-wise MM-RAG benchmark.

claim_closure.claim: Every retained hop is necessary and non-redundant.
claim_closure.method_response: Util(t), Nav(t), hop shrinkage and redundancy checks operationalize necessity.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Quality scores and unique-graph filtering support the procedure, but threshold values and per-hop pass rates are absent.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers hop-wise attribution without adding validation detail.

claim_closure.claim: Final-answer accuracy alone is insufficient for long agentic chains.
claim_closure.method_response: F1/ΔF1/Golden F1/LLJ plus HPS/RD separate answer and chain behavior.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3, Figure 5 and case studies expose retrieval, omission and modality errors beyond final answer.

claim_closure.claim: Five topology definitions form a complete canonical basis.
claim_closure.method_response: Linear chains are split by initiation/modality and Forked chains by branch modality.
claim_closure.evidence_response: M.2 gives a textual exhaustion argument under Linear/Forked and one-branch assumptions; no external graph enumeration is needed for the stated restricted space.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: M.3 states completeness under the assumptions.

claim_closure.claim: An agentic pipeline can adapt modality and stopping across long chains.
claim_closure.method_response: Three-module loop generates sub-query/action, retrieves top-1 evidence, reasons and stops/continues.
claim_closure.evidence_response: RQ1–RQ5 evaluate its chain length, modality coverage, HPS/RD and error behavior.

claim_closure.claim: Main failures arise during retrieval planning and evidence acquisition.
claim_closure.method_response: Actions and retrieved evidence are logged; HPS/RD and modality coverage localize steps.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Retrieval-Failure and Step-Omission dominate, but error labels are assigned by Gemini-2.5-Pro and do not establish exclusive causal attribution.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion treats retrieval fidelity as central bottleneck.

evidence.anchor: chosen modality and evidence are logged
retrieval and planning are earlier failure points

claim_closure.claim: SEARCH-ALIGN improves open-source MLLM planning and retrieval fidelity.
claim_closure.method_response: HAVE-verified chains are converted into thought-augmented conversations and SFT.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3, Figure 7 and Table 14 show gains, but comparison is before/after without reported seeds or an independent causal design.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion presents MC-SEARCH as a resource; no stronger causal claim is added.

claim_closure.claim: MC-SEARCH is the first benchmark of this kind.
claim_closure.method_response: Related work provides taxonomy and nearest-neighbor contrasts.
claim_closure.evidence_response: The PDF does not contain an exhaustive literature-search protocol that can verify a universal first claim.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion avoids adding new novelty evidence.

claim_closure.method_response: Unique graph filtering, HPS/RD and LLJ define process and answer checks.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Cross-model and human consistency support evaluator reliability, while generator dependence and exact-match boundaries remain.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls for principled evaluation standards.

measurement_disagreements.description: 自动总词数 14,894 把正文、references、目录和附录合并；本深读将页面边界和模块词数作为估计，不把自动总数当作正文词数。

final_judgment.single_storyline: 论文把 multimodal agentic search 从 final-answer accuracy 改写为对必要证据、模态动作、长链长度和停止行为的过程评测：MC-SEARCH 提供五类 topology/chain，HAVE 过滤，HPS/RD/LLJ 诊断，SEARCH-ALIGN 将 verified chain 用于 SFT。[p. 3–7, §§2–3]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留 five topology 定义、Util/Nav、三模块 pipeline、五个 RQ、Table 3、Figures 3–5 和 Ethics 边界，足以支撑 benchmark/诊断的决策闭环。[p. 3–10, §§2–6]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: fixed baselines、数据/质量统计、评审一致性、fine-tuning hyperparameters、soft HPS、top-k、case study、理论 case split 和 N–P prompts 迁入 p.20–35；正文自足于主要判断，但复现和评审边界依赖附录。[p. 20–35, Appendices D–P]
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 将构造与执行并列，Table 3 以 topology 分组并列 answer/chain 指标，Figures 3–5 紧跟 RQ2–RQ5，形成对象—过程—诊断的可扫读结构。[p. 3, 7–9]
final_judgment.largest_gap: faithful evaluation、first benchmark 与 SEARCH-ALIGN 能力改善分别依赖生成模型过滤、LLJ 评审和前后训练对照；PDF 没有 random seeds、完整 causal design 或人工全量标注，因此这些主张弱于 benchmark 构造事实。[p. 4–7, 23–25, 35]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Agentic/long-horizon 论文应把每个决策单位的必要证据、动作模态、链长度与停止行为做成 claim-bearing artifacts，并同时展示 fixed baseline、过程错误和失败链。[p. 4–9, 20–21, 29]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则适合有离散检索动作、可标注 intermediate evidence 且错误沿 hop 累积的 agentic QA；不直接覆盖连续控制、无可验证中间证据或无法定义唯一 hop 的联合检索任务。[p. 3–6, 30, 34]
